judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard covenant chapeau; "so long as any credit hereunder shall be available and until payment in full of the Obligations" is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Section 7 chapeau (c319) adds "until termination of this Agreement" whereas this one does not, a small asymmetry between the affirmative and negative covenant periods.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "information as from time to time reasonably may be requested by Lender" is open-ended but the core obligation is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.2's reporting requirements and 5.6's records representation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reporting table is badly mangled in the executed text, with the timing column interleaved into the item descriptions, so which frequency attaches to which report is genuinely hard to read; item (h) is also an unbounded "such other reports ... as Lender may request".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The daily/monthly deadlines here must be squared with 3.3(f)'s requirement of a "current" Borrowing Base Certificate at each Advance and with 6.3's monthly financial reporting; the mangled table makes that harder.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains several mechanical slips — "with 30 days after the end of each month" for "within", and a cross-reference rendered "Sections 7.16 and 217" — inside an otherwise detailed reporting covenant; clause (h) is an unbounded catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It calls Sections 7.16 and 7.17 the "applicable financial covenants" although 7.17 is a collateral-quality limit, and it requires an unqualified audit opinion measured against those same covenants; also relevant is 7.16(b)'s defective ratio.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A placeholder with no content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.2 lists the covenants whose breach is an Event of Default and omits 6.4 while including 6.15, which is also "Intentionally Omitted"; the inconsistency is cosmetic.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading is mis-numbered "6.3" although the section is 6.5, and clause (a) stacks "commercially reasonable efforts ... to the extent that it is commercially reasonable to do so and in a commercially reasonable manner", a circular triple use of the same standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The duty to collect is expressly "Subject to Section 4.8", which allocates servicing to Borrowers or Servicer; and 9.1(e)/(o) let Lender take over — the three fit together but only with care.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "necessary or useful in the proper conduct of its business" and "material leases" are soft, but this is standard maintenance covenant language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.17 Leases and 6.11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and definite, with express Permitted Protest carve-outs; "proof satisfactory to Lender" is the only soft element.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.1(i), the Permitted Protest definition and Section 10's self-help right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "all other hazards and risks as ordinarily are insured against by other Persons engaged in the same or similar businesses" is a general catch-all after specific perils, and "as sole loss payee ... or additional insured, as appropriate" leaves the choice unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.1(g) and 6.8(b)-(c); Section 10(c) gives Lender force-placement rights if this covenant is breached.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear $50,000 threshold and disbursement mechanics; "staged payment terms reasonably satisfactory to Lender" is the only soft term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.8(a) and 2.3(b)'s application rules; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "concurrent in form or contributing in the event of loss" is technical insurance language, but its meaning is settled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.8(a); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear location covenant with a 30-day notice amendment mechanic, though "Schedule 5.7" is cited without the subsection letter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires a Collateral Access Agreement for any new location, which sits against 5.5's and 7.15's public-warehouse proviso permitting storage where access has merely been assigned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Compliance is qualified by the Material Adverse Change standard, importing that vague term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 5.3, which represents compliance with all applicable laws without any materiality qualifier — the covenant is markedly softer than the representation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short, definite, with a Permitted Protest carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.17 and the Permitted Protest definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Introduces separateness covenants using "all reasonable steps, including ... all steps that Lender may from time to time reasonably request" — an open-ended obligation and a corporate-formalities requirement applied to LLCs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The separateness regime sits awkwardly with 2.13's joint and several liability and with 7.13's permitted affiliate transactions and management/servicing arrangements with Bar-K.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "observe all corporate formalities as a distinct entity" is vague as applied to a California LLC, which has no corporate formalities as such.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Governing Documents definition (c081) contemplates LLC operating agreements, so the corporate vocabulary is a mismatch with the actual entities.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear separateness requirement for books and assets.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.1 and the Books definition; note that 6.12(b) is missing from the sampled sequence, which suggests a gap in the executed document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The double exception ("except as herein specifically otherwise provided" and "except for the Cash Management Accounts or as required by any written agreement between Fund and an Account Debtor") makes the scope of the no-commingling prohibition hard to fix; the closing words appear to prohibit maintaining any bank account at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read literally it would bar the Designated Account required by 2.8 and the Escrow Accounts required by 2.6(e) and 6.17, so it cannot be applied without harmonising against those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four enumerated environmental covenants, each with a defined trigger; "reportable quantity" is externally defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.14 and the Environmental Lien/Remedial Action definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear notification duty with an explicit statement that notification does not cure or amend.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits deliberately against 5.19 Complete Disclosure and the various "as updated from time to time" schedules, which it prevents from being self-amending.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A placeholder with no content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.2(a) nonetheless makes failure to observe Section 6.15 an Event of Default, an internal oddity since there is nothing to observe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "To the extent necessary to comply with Section 4.2" imports that section's $250,000,000 threshold, but the covenant then speaks of delivering "all original promissory notes", which is broader — the two halves point different ways.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.2 requires delivery of only enough notes to reach $250,000,000 absent a default, while Eligible Notes Receivable clause (r) and 3.1(t) impose delivery requirements on every note; the three are hard to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear deposit obligation with an inclusive list of escrow categories.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires deposit into "a Deposit Account that is subject to a perfected Lender's Lien", whereas 2.6(e) requires Escrow Accounts at Cash Management Banks under Cash Management Agreements; the two describe the same duty differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The covenant requires escrow instructions calling for the documents "listed in Section 3.3(z)", but Section 3.3 has only clauses (a) through (f) — the cross-reference has no referent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The intended reference is presumably 3.1(t), whose document list is the one used elsewhere (4.2, 8.17); as written the covenant cannot be applied without repairing it against those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard negative-covenant chapeau; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs "until termination of this Agreement and payment in full", while the affirmative covenant chapeau (c295) omits the termination limb; a minor asymmetry.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The lettering runs (a) through (f) and then jumps to "(z) endorsement of instruments or other payment items for deposit", a plain mechanical error in the enumeration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (b) permits Indebtedness "set forth on Schedule 5.20", tying the covenant to a schedule described in 5.20 as a Closing Date snapshot; Approved Debt and Subordinated Debt in (d)-(e) then interact with 7.7 and 7.10.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short prohibition keyed to the defined Permitted Liens, with a well-drawn replacement-Lien parenthetical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its operation depends entirely on the Permitted Liens definition (c130), whose clause (c) proviso about Approved Debt Liens is grammatically broken.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad prohibition (including any amendment of Governing Documents) with a single exception for a Permitted Reorganization.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exception depends on the Permitted Reorganization definition (c133), which is anchored to an extrinsic written description; whether a given restructuring qualifies is the crux.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "except incidental to a Permitted Reorganization" appears twice in one sentence, making the drafting clumsy but the meaning clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same dependence on c133 as 7.3(a); consistent in structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "all or any substantial part of its assets" is an undefined quantum, and the clause sits directly against 7.4, which prohibits disposing of "any" assets.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.4 (c325) prohibits any disposition other than Permitted Dispositions, so 7.3(c)'s narrower "substantial part" test is redundant at best and inconsistent at worst.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An absolute prohibition on disposing of "any" assets subject only to Permitted Dispositions; short and stark.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps 7.3(c) and 4.1's last sentence, and its practical content is set entirely by the Permitted Dispositions definition (c127) and the release mechanic in 4.9(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The prohibition covers names, EINs, organizational numbers and state of organization, but the proviso permits only name changes on notice — the mismatch leaves the other changes absolutely barred, perhaps unintentionally.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.9's amendment mechanic covers locations and chief executive offices but not organizational identity; 5.7 fixes those details on schedules with no update mechanic.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence begins with three carve-outs before reaching the prohibition, and "the curtailment in the origination of new loans" is an unbounded exception that could permit the business to be wound down entirely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That exception sits uneasily with 7.14's use-of-proceeds contemplation of making new Eligible Notes Receivable and with the Triggering Event definition's $500,000,000 portfolio floor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (c) prohibits amendments "in any manner that would be adverse to any Borrower" — an odd formulation, since a covenant for Lender's benefit would normally bar amendments adverse to Lender.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The opening carve-out for payments permitted by 7.10 and refinancings under 7.1(f) ties this covenant to those provisions; the Approved Debt payment permission is the operative escape.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One line resting on the defined term; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on Change of Control (c044), which keys to Permitted Holders (c128) and to Subsidiaries in existence at the Closing Date; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "advance notice to, and consent by, the Lender" specifies no notice period and no standard for consent, and "in any material respect" is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Borrower's Required Procedures definition (c033) already requires prior written Lender approval in Lender's sole discretion for any amendment, so this covenant duplicates and slightly contradicts that standard.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exception permitting distributions "to the extent required or permitted by Fund's Governing Documents" is an unbounded carve-out that lets an amendable extrinsic document define what the covenant allows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against the Restricted Payments definition (c142), 7.7 and the Permitted Reorganization machinery, this exception could permit the very member redemptions the covenant appears designed to control; the cross-reference is also mis-rendered as "Section 6.30b)".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single long sentence combining a fiscal-year/accounting-method restriction with an accountant-access condition; awkward but comprehensible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 1.2, 6.3's accountant-consultation rights and the GAAP definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short prohibition with two exceptions keyed to defined terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on Permitted Investments (c129) and Permitted Reorganization (c133); the reorganization exception is unqualified and broad.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (c) forbids "any other transaction" with an Affiliate except those that are "in the ordinary course", "upon fair and reasonable terms", "fully disclosed to Lender" and "no less favorable ... than would be obtained in an arm's length transaction" — a general catch-all after two specific prohibitions, resting on four undefined evaluative standards; the opening sentence about forming Subsidiaries also sits oddly under the section heading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its exceptions run to Permitted Dispositions (c127), Permitted Investments (c129), Section 7.10 payments and Permitted Reorganizations (c133), and "Affiliate" carries a special 10% deeming rule under c008 expressly "for purposes of ... Section 7.13"; whether transfers to affiliated entities were permitted turns on how all of these fit together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (b)(ii) permits proceeds to be used for "working capital and general corporate needs ... including funding of its obligations with respect to any Investor Membership Interests or pursuant to a Permitted Reorganization" — an elastic permission whose outer edge is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That permission has to be read against 7.10's Restricted Payments prohibition and the Approved Debt/Subordinated Note machinery, since funding member withdrawals with Advance proceeds is both contemplated here and constrained there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A prohibition immediately undercut by a proviso permitting public-warehouse storage of certain loan files; "loan files that do not include original promissory notes, Lien instruments, or assignments" is a workable but fine distinction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates almost verbatim the proviso in 5.5 (c267) and interacts with 6.9's Collateral Access Agreement requirement; the three are close but not identical.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed dollar covenant tested monthly; arithmetically definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Tangible Net Worth (c157) adds Subordinated Debt back to equity, so the reorganization notes can preserve compliance even as members are cashed out — a significant interaction with 7.10 and c153.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "a Senior Leverage Ratio (expressed as a percentage) that is of no greater than nine-tenths of one percent (0.9%)" contains a stray "is of" and, more seriously, a percentage that cannot be right for a ratio of Obligations to Tangible Net Worth.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: With a $50,000,000 Maximum Revolver Amount against $600,000,000 of required Tangible Net Worth, the ratio would be about 8%, so a 0.9% ceiling is unattainable and irreconcilable with 2.1(a), c114 and 7.16(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear 25% monthly test; the only softness is imported from the Defaulted Note Receivable definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because "Defaulted Note Receivable" (c056) depends on what Administrative Borrower or Lender "deems" non-performing, the covenant's numerator is partly within the parties' control — a real dependency on that definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Payment default stated plainly and comprehensively; no grace period, but that is a choice rather than an ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Obligations definition (c121) and 2.4's promise to pay; note Bank Product Obligations are within "Obligations" here but excluded elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated list in (a) includes Section 6.15, which is "Intentionally Omitted", and omits 6.4; clause (c) is a residual for "any Section ... other than a Section that is expressly dealt with elsewhere in this Section 8.2", a general-after-specific structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The tiered cure periods (none, 15 days, 20 Business Days) must be mapped onto the covenant sections, and the reference to conditions subsequent in 3.2 duplicates 3.2's own statement that failure "constitut[es] an Event of Default" without any cure — a direct tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "any material portion" is undefined and "comes into the possession of any third Person" is extremely broad, capturing innocuous events.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It would literally be triggered by delivery of notes to a custodian, which 4.2 expressly contemplates; that needs harmonising.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Insolvency Proceeding (c090) and 9.1's automatic acceleration on 8.4/8.5 events.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "not timely controverted" is a term with no fixed meaning in the document and no stated period, unlike the 45-day test in the next clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent in structure with 8.4 and with 9.1's automatic acceleration provision; the undefined timing standard is the only soft point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "all or any material part of its business affairs" is undefined but the trigger (a court order) is objective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps 3.3(c)'s no-injunction condition; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long and technical ("whether choate or otherwise") but the trigger is objective and tied to delinquency.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.7, the Permitted Protest definition and Permitted Liens (b); the Permitted Protest carve-out is not repeated here, which is a small gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed $200,000 threshold; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Permitted Liens (j) excludes judgment Liens that are "not an Event of Default hereunder", so the two provisions define each other circularly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (z) — "any other agreement ... the termination of which is reasonably likely to result in a Material Adverse Change" — is a general catch-all after two specifics, and the qualifier attaches to termination rather than to default.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (x)'s reference to "capital obligations to any member or former member in connection with their Investor Membership Interests" interacts directly with 7.10 and the Approved Debt/Subordinated Note machinery, where such obligations are expressly contemplated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear trigger with an exception keyed to the subordination provisions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 7.7(b) and 7.10(b), which permit payments to the extent the Subordination Agreement allows.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "any material misstatement or misrepresentation" in any "warranty, representation, statement, or Record" made by any employee or agent is very broad, with no knowledge or notice qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5's representations are already qualified "in all material respects", so this clause layers a second materiality test; 6.14 requires correction but says correction does not cure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear trigger; the Validity Agreement itself is not attached, so what "terminated by operation of law" means depends on that document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Validity Agreement and Validity Agreement Party definitions (c162, c163) and 3.1(b)(iii).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "an individual with comparable education, experience and other qualifications acceptable to Lender" combines an objective comparison with an unqualified acceptability veto.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Executive Officer" (c075) is a fixed list of five named individuals, so the clause is triggered by any of them leaving Manager or Servicer even though Servicer is not a Borrower and is excluded from "Subsidiary" (c155).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Well-drawn, with an express carve-out for dispositions permitted under the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That carve-out ties directly to Permitted Dispositions (c127) and the release mechanic in 4.9(b) (c260) — if a sale is not "in accordance with the terms of this Agreement", the loss of the Lien would itself be a default.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite, though it depends on a document not reproduced here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Servicing Agreement is a Loan Document under c110, so its breach would in any event fall within 8.2(a)'s "comparable provision" language — a duplication.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Makes the default turn on any provision "that Lender in its Permitted Discretion deems to be material", a wholly Lender-side determination, and the clause ends mid-sentence with "or."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps 8.14's failure-of-Lien default and 5.9(d)'s enforceability representation; the truncated ending suggests text is missing from the executed document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "otherwise reasonably acceptable to Lender" qualifies an otherwise precise $250,000,000 test, and the parenthetical about substitutions is compressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It polices the same threshold as 3.1(t), 3.3(e) and 4.2, but 4.2 requires that threshold only "so long as no Event of Default has occurred", so the three provisions state the requirement in different terms.
